# Beyond the GRPO name: advantage scales, clipping units, and train–rollout mismatch

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/post-training/policy-optimization.md) · English

Updated 2026-11-23 · 66 topic entries / 18 representative comparisons

The GRPO family differs in how rewards become advantages, which likelihood ratio is clipped, and which distribution produced samples. Dr. GRPO, DAPO, GSPO, and TIS/IcePop modify different parts; not every ratio is the same off-policy correction.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

## Mechanism comparison {#comparison}

Axes: Advantage scale: group mean, group standard deviation, and length normalization · Update unit: token surrogate or sequence ratio · Sampling validity: zero-variance groups and dynamic resampling · Distribution roles: current training policy, old training policy, and rollout engine

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Identify the numerator and denominator before discussing stability

GSPO aggregates response log-ratios of current versus old policy. TIS and IcePop compare probabilities under the same weights across training and rollout engines. One controls update size and the other corrects implementation mismatch. A training loop can need both; neither automatically covers the other's bias.

Sources: [GSPO](../../../../post-training/2507.18071-gspo/README-en.md) · [TIS](../../../../post-training/web-2025-tis/README-en.md) · [IcePop](../../../../post-training/2510.18855-icepop/README-en.md)

### Normalization changes weights, not missing signals

GRPO standard deviation, its removal in Dr. GRPO, and DAPO aggregation over valid tokens alter sample contributions. An all-right or all-wrong group can still have no direction after centering. Dynamic sampling controls whether such groups reach updates. Count discarded generation work, not just optimizer steps.

Sources: [DeepSeekMath / GRPO](../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en.md) · [Dr. GRPO](../../../../post-training/2503.20783-dr-grpo/README-en.md) · [DAPO](../../../../post-training/2503.14476-dapo/README-en.md)

### Choose the update event before clipping: text and decisions are different variables

GRPO/GSPO mainly change advantages or ratio units of an existing text policy. RLiD first changes the probability event to a compiled menu action. Its Rao–Blackwell account conditions on alternative wordings of the same action within one text policy; it does not prove a separately trained LDM stronger. Afterstate menus, memory provenance, label calibration, and interface matching must be specified first. Sharing a PPO formula does not remove these differences.

Sources: [RLiD: Reinforcement Learning in the Decision Plane for Language Agents and LLMs](../../../../post-training/2611.02455-rlid/README-en.md) · [DeepSeekMath / GRPO](../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en.md) · [GSPO](../../../../post-training/2507.18071-gspo/README-en.md)

### Locate the off-policy mismatch before choosing a correction

TIS compares probabilities from training and rollout engines at the same weights, addressing numerical implementation mismatch. Ex-Retrace compares target and behavior policies and builds a multi-step value target by mixing whole excursion durations. Both use importance ratios, but their conditional variables and update objects differ. A tokenwise trainer/rollout ratio cannot replace an excursion prefix, and excursion TD does not remove an LM engine's numerical mismatch.

Sources: [Off-policy Learning with Excursion Policies](../../../../post-training/2611.13275-excursion-td/README-en.md) · [TIS](../../../../post-training/web-2025-tis/README-en.md)

### The old policy controls sampling ratios; the KL reference sets the optimization anchor

GRPO uses old-policy ratios and group advantages, alongside a separate reference KL. APMD resets that KL anchor across outer iterations, accumulating progress under strong local constraints. Refreshing the sampling old policy does not establish APMD's reference condition. Group centering also does not remove Kimi's squared-KL mean-baseline bias relative to the mirror target. Finite identities cannot replace realizability checks or sampling-error analysis for real LLMs.

Sources: [A Theory of Policy Optimization in Post-Training: Coverage Collapse and Reference Resets](../../../../post-training/2611.14467-apmd-reference-reset/README-en.md) · [DeepSeekMath / GRPO](../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en.md)

### Gradient membership and advantage scale are independent design axes

Dr. GRPO keeps centered rewards while removing group-std and length biases. LGPO supplies no new reward estimator; it removes whole-response gradients above a current-policy mean-logp threshold. Renormalizing survivors changes step scale by acceptance rate, not by the same operation as removing std. Comparisons or combinations must fix sampling policies, advantage scales, valid tokens and the all-response denominator. The authors' two-H100 timing is not local acceleration evidence.

Sources: [Is the Importance Ratio Necessary for Stable Reinforcement Learning in LLMs?](../../../../post-training/2611.15404-lgpo/README-en.md) · [Dr. GRPO](../../../../post-training/2503.20783-dr-grpo/README-en.md)

### Preserving multiplier scale and calibrating cost are separate requirements

Dr. GRPO-style unscaled advantages prevent total-reward group std from canceling multipliers, but biased scorer means can still saturate or deactivate the dual. Safety as a Budget maps only penalties/control using training trajectories while raw base rewards preserve within-group differences. PAV plateaus, data separation, EMA state and interpolation need explicit contracts. Monotonicity is not calibration, and per-objective standardized results are not local unscaled outcomes.

Sources: [Safety as a Budget: Calibrating the Control Channel of Constrained GRPO for Vision-Language Models](../../../../post-training/2611.16628-safety-budget-cgrpo/README-en.md) · [Dr. GRPO](../../../../post-training/2503.20783-dr-grpo/README-en.md)

### Why must a rollout not certify itself using a subspace containing itself?

An outlier may create its own direction. LOO removes the row, centers the others and truncates their SVD using group effective rank before measuring held-out projected energy. GRPO uses group reward mean/variance. SpeCal additionally uses pooled hidden-state spectra and LOO support, with batch/group RMS calibration. Replacing a reward standard deviation cannot reproduce it. Local boundary: Centered Gram spectrum of normalized response representations, mass times effective-rank band-pass, denoised LOO-SVD support and two-level RMS advantage calibration.

Sources: [SpeCal: Spectral Calibration for Unsupervised RLVR](../../../../post-training/2611.20691-specal/README-en.md) · [DeepSeekMath / GRPO](../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en.md)

### Can TIS and reverse-KL silently share an already clipped ratio?

No. Sample and auxiliary reward ratios are independently computed and TIS-clipped. The KL term has its own cap. Coefficients are detached in the score surrogate and behavior remains fixed within an inner fit. RSC uses reverse KL to the behavior distribution that generated the batch and refreshes this reference with the sampler. GRPO commonly uses a more fixed pretrained reference. Behavior probabilities cannot be replaced by another reference's probabilities in importance ratios. Local boundary: Weighted score centers from independent auxiliary actions, detached TIS weights and reverse-KL gradient estimator with an independent KL cap; not reward centering.

Sources: [Regularized Score Centering](../../../../post-training/2611.21791-regularized-score-centering/README-en.md) · [DeepSeekMath / GRPO](../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en.md)

### Why update steering before the model each step?

The steering loss must fit the model that generated the current hinted/plain samples. Updating the model first makes that relation stale. The final step updates steering only, avoiding a stale returned vector. GRPO removes the critic but still relies on relative rewards within a group. ASH normalizes hinted/plain groups separately, trains activation steering before GRPO and skips the final model update to avoid a stale vector. Existing candidate GRPO success is not hint-free generation capability. Local boundary: Review steering-before-GRPO order, separately normalized hint/plain advantages and final-step no-model-update rule; a DPO formula alone is not an implementation.

Sources: [Get Hint-Augmented GRPO Done Right Through Activation Steering](../../../../post-training/2611.23124-ash-hint-steering/README-en.md) · [DeepSeekMath / GRPO](../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en.md)

### Can LED directly replace ORL residual learning?

ORL learns on model-induced residual states and requires its own inference chain. LED changes discrete length alignment and edit supervision using LCS targets. Both address training/inference state mismatch, but residual distributions are not edit actions, and their separate local boundaries do not combine into a complete model. No. The program executes deterministic LCS and edit transitions, with a clean target only for label construction. It has no model prediction, diffusion SFT, multi-stage training or benchmark answer generation, so it is an L1 mechanism diagnostic.

Sources: [Beyond Replacement: Levenshtein Editing for Diffusion Language Models](../../../../post-training/2611.23750-led-edits/README-en.md) · [On-Policy Residual Learning for Diffusion Language Models](../../../../post-training/2610.20687-orl-diffusion/README-en.md)

### Is DFRL another optimizer replacing RLOO?

Existing RLOO treats a complete response as an action, baselines its reward against the other responses, and may add KL shaping. DFRL specifies downstream realized decision cost as feedback; its RLOO analysis cancels the common hindsight constant, and batch-switch reward correction reduces expensive feedback calls. RLOO does not define business regret automatically, and DFRL does not make arbitrary normalization, clipping or candidate-dependent baselines unbiased. They concern an objective/feedback pipeline and an estimator, not mutually exclusive algorithms. Solving every exact problem and masking afterward does not save solves. The local I=0 branch never calls the lazy callback; I=1 calls the whole-batch supplier once. Require0<p<=1 and handle variance and overflow at small p explicitly.

Sources: [Decision-Focused Reinforcement Learning for LLM Post-Training](../../../../post-training/2611.25597-dfrl/README-en.md) · [RLOO](../../../../post-training/2402.14740-rloo/README-en.md)

### Does RLOO's constant cancellation remove retokenization drift?

DFRL changes downstream decision-cost feedback, and RLOO cancels a shared within-instance constant. This paper holds rewards and advantages fixed and asks how encoding changes score gradients. Baseline cancellation does not equalize different token-path Jacobians; unchanged rewards do not imply unchanged updates. Sources: Section2, Eqs.1–2; Section4, Proposition1; AppendixE. Sampling ab gives the coarse full-score step λ(e_ab−π). The fine policy updates only the root and a-successor rows, leaving the b row and ba/bb odds fixed. When π(ba)≠π(bb), agreement requires a zero step. The uniform symmetric exception violates that premise, so a universal no-nonzero-step claim would be false. AppendixE separately describes a weaker sampled-logit-only simulator; local code uses the full softmax gradient instead.

Sources: [How Far Does Lossless Re-tokenization Move an RLVR Update?](../../../../post-training/2611.27083-retokenization-update/README-en.md) · [Decision-Focused Reinforcement Learning for LLM Post-Training](../../../../post-training/2611.25597-dfrl/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Why does lower variance after text-to-action marginalization not imply RLiD wins every task over reasoning-token policies? {#cross-same-policy-marginalization-not-new-model-win}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** The result fixes one text policy and action-dependent advantages, preserving expected updates while removing realization variance. Real LDMs have different parameterizations and training paths, while reasoning adds computation. Temporal credit and menu interfaces remain separate. The paper's Qwen3.5-2B ARC result still favors token policies; that counterexample must be retained.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: Two wordings of open from one policy can be marginalized. Replacing it with another label-only network lies outside that same-policy identity.

    Sources: [RLiD: Reinforcement Learning in the Decision Plane for Language Agents and LLMs](../../../../post-training/2611.02455-rlid/README-en.md) · [DeepSeekMath / GRPO](../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en.md)

### If all four responses are wrong, does changing GRPO to Dr. GRPO create a learning direction? {#cross-all-failed-group}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Not when rewards remain identical: removing standard deviation leaves centered advantages zero. Dr. GRPO changes scale bias; DAPO filters such groups and samples again. If budget never yields distinguishable outcomes, improve exploration or supervision rather than relabel normalization.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: With all rewards zero, subtracting the mean still yields zero. A constant denominator does not make one trajectory better.

    Sources: [DeepSeekMath / GRPO](../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en.md) · [Dr. GRPO](../../../../post-training/2503.20783-dr-grpo/README-en.md) · [DAPO](../../../../post-training/2503.14476-dapo/README-en.md)

### Is GSPO equivalent to clipping each token with PPO and then averaging? {#cross-sequence-ratio-not-token-average}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. GSPO aggregates log-ratios into one response ratio before clipping. Per-token clipping applies nonlinear selection first. Averaging and clipping do not commute, so outlier tokens have different effects. Sequence rewards do not mathematically require one unique surrogate.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: With one very high ratio and other ratios near one, per-token clipping can clip just that token; GSPO assigns the aggregate weight to the entire response.

    Sources: [DeepSeekMath / GRPO](../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en.md) · [GSPO](../../../../post-training/2507.18071-gspo/README-en.md) · [DAPO](../../../../post-training/2503.14476-dapo/README-en.md)

### How do TIS and IcePop handle a very small engine ratio, and is that policy staleness? {#cross-tis-versus-icepop}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** TIS caps only large ratios and retains the small one. IcePop zeros its policy gradient below the lower bound. Both address engine mismatch, not drift between current and old sampling weights. Masking is not standard PPO clipping or a cure for stale policies.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: Different kernels giving different probabilities at identical weights is an engine issue. Sampling from weights several updates old introduces separate policy staleness.

    Sources: [TIS](../../../../post-training/web-2025-tis/README-en.md) · [IcePop](../../../../post-training/2510.18855-icepop/README-en.md) · [GSPO](../../../../post-training/2507.18071-gspo/README-en.md)

### Can TIS's one-sided ratio truncation directly replace Ex-Retrace? {#cross-engine-ratio-versus-excursion}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. TIS corrects training/rollout-engine probability mismatch. Ex-Retrace defines a multi-step value target between target and behavior policies, mixing target-then-behavior durations. First identify each ratio's numerator, denominator, conditioning variables and update object.

    **Illustrative example:** For example, two engines assigning a token probabilities .2 and .1 give a TIS ratio of 2. An Ex-Retrace ratio instead compares target/behavior action probabilities at a state and additionally needs gamma, lambda, beta and subsequent Q values.

    Sources: [Off-policy Learning with Excursion Policies](../../../../post-training/2611.13275-excursion-td/README-en.md) · [TIS](../../../../post-training/web-2025-tis/README-en.md)

### Why does periodically refreshing GRPO's old policy not establish APMD reference resets? {#cross-cross-old-policy-versus-kl-anchor-reset}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** The old policy records behavior probabilities in a ratio denominator; the KL reference is a regularization anchor. They may update separately. APMD also requires an inner-approximation condition, so calling both old models does not make them equivalent.

    **Illustrative example:** Refresh the old policy before each sampled batch but keep penalizing KL to the original base: that reference is still fixed. APMD instead anchors the next outer round at the latest pi_t.

    Sources: [A Theory of Policy Optimization in Post-Training: Coverage Collapse and Reference Resets](../../../../post-training/2611.14467-apmd-reference-reset/README-en.md) · [DeepSeekMath / GRPO](../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en.md)

### Should LGPO divide by survivors to compensate when half the responses are gated? {#cross-cross-nov15-lgpo-normalization}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Not under this fidelity contract. The expectation averages all responses and assigns zero to gated ones. Survivor division increases the effective step size. Dr. GRPO's removed std does not establish equivalence for this denominator change.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: four responses, two retained and total contribution six give -6/4, not -6/2.

    Sources: [Is the Importance Ratio Necessary for Stable Reinforcement Learning in LLMs?](../../../../post-training/2611.15404-lgpo/README-en.md) · [Dr. GRPO](../../../../post-training/2503.20783-dr-grpo/README-en.md)

### Does removing std in a Dr. GRPO-style update make the safety budget a true event rate? {#cross-cross-nov15-budget-std}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. It preserves gradient scaling by the multiplier, but the budget still reads scorer means. Uncorrected bias can stabilize the controller at the wrong level. Independent labels, training-only fitting, held-out evaluation and explicit state remain necessary.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: gradient scaling is preserved, but a scorer that always understates harmfulness can still drive lambda to zero.

    Sources: [Safety as a Budget: Calibrating the Control Channel of Constrained GRPO for Vision-Language Models](../../../../post-training/2611.16628-safety-budget-cgrpo/README-en.md) · [Dr. GRPO](../../../../post-training/2503.20783-dr-grpo/README-en.md)

### What is added beyond GRPO group standardization? {#cross-nov18-specal}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** GRPO uses group reward mean/variance. SpeCal additionally uses pooled hidden-state spectra and LOO support, with batch/group RMS calibration. Replacing a reward standard deviation cannot reproduce it.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: scaling one representation by seven is removed by L2 normalization; changing its direction changes the spectrum and support.

    Sources: [SpeCal: Spectral Calibration for Unsupervised RLVR](../../../../post-training/2611.20691-specal/README-en.md) · [DeepSeekMath / GRPO](../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en.md)

### How does its KL differ from ordinary GRPO reference KL? {#cross-nov18-regularized-score-centering}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** RSC uses reverse KL to the behavior distribution that generated the batch and refreshes this reference with the sampler. GRPO commonly uses a more fixed pretrained reference. Behavior probabilities cannot be replaced by another reference's probabilities in importance ratios.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: with behavior .2 and reference .1, the importance-ratio denominator remains .2.

    Sources: [Regularized Score Centering](../../../../post-training/2611.21791-regularized-score-centering/README-en.md) · [DeepSeekMath / GRPO](../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en.md)

### Does an existing GRPO implementation establish ASH hint-free behavior transfer? {#cross-nov18-ash-hint-steering}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** GRPO removes the critic but still relies on relative rewards within a group. ASH normalizes hinted/plain groups separately, trains activation steering before GRPO and skips the final model update to avoid a stale vector. Existing candidate GRPO success is not hint-free generation capability.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: separately normalizing hinted/plain groups still requires actual activation-vector training before the model and no model update on the final step.

    Sources: [Get Hint-Augmented GRPO Done Right Through Activation Steering](../../../../post-training/2611.23124-ash-hint-steering/README-en.md) · [DeepSeekMath / GRPO](../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en.md)

### Can LED directly replace ORL residual learning? {#cross-nov19-led-edits}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. LED reconstructs discrete position-level edit supervision. ORL transports model residual distributions and collects induced states online. Shared exposure-bias motivation does not imply equal states, objectives or inference engines.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: an LCS Ins label supplies neither a full next-round residual probability tensor nor a trained diffusion model.

    Sources: [Beyond Replacement: Levenshtein Editing for Diffusion Language Models](../../../../post-training/2611.23750-led-edits/README-en.md) · [On-Policy Residual Learning for Diffusion Language Models](../../../../post-training/2610.20687-orl-diffusion/README-en.md)

### Is DFRL another optimizer replacing RLOO? {#cross-nov21-dfrl}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. DFRL specifies a decision-regret objective and feedback, while RLOO can estimate its score gradient. The shared hindsight optimum cancels from the baseline; arbitrary advantage standardization or KL shaping changes the analyzed objective or update.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: costs2 and5 yield advantages3 and minus3. Subtracting the same hindsight cost1 leaves them unchanged, avoiding another solve under observed parameters.

    Sources: [Decision-Focused Reinforcement Learning for LLM Post-Training](../../../../post-training/2611.25597-dfrl/README-en.md) · [RLOO](../../../../post-training/2402.14740-rloo/README-en.md)

### Does RLOO's constant cancellation remove retokenization drift? {#cross-nov23-retokenization-update}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. DFRL's shared hindsight-cost constant cancels within advantages. Retokenization changes the score-gradient multiplied by those advantages. Cancellation on the reward axis is not parameterization invariance.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: advantage1 multiplying two different score vectors still gives different updates. Subtracting10 from both rewards does not align those vectors.

    Sources: [How Far Does Lossless Re-tokenization Move an RLVR Update?](../../../../post-training/2611.27083-retokenization-update/README-en.md) · [Decision-Focused Reinforcement Learning for LLM Post-Training](../../../../post-training/2611.25597-dfrl/README-en.md)

## Update log {#updates}

Updates record new approaches, changed trade-offs, and follow-up evidence.

**2026-11-23** · DFRL changes downstream decision-cost feedback, and RLOO cancels a shared within-instance constant. This paper holds rewards and advantages fixed and asks how encoding changes score gradients. Baseline cancellation does not equalize different token-path Jacobians; unchanged rewards do not imply unchanged updates. L1 core-mechanism component, diagnostic only; not LLM capability or a full reproduction. CPU only, with no CUDA path or Evolve promotion evidence. Full experiments are high-cost and not reproduced, review DONE.

Affected: [How Far Does Lossless Re-tokenization Move an RLVR Update?](../../../../post-training/2611.27083-retokenization-update/README-en.md) · [Decision-Focused Reinforcement Learning for LLM Post-Training](../../../../post-training/2611.25597-dfrl/README-en.md)

**2026-11-21** · Pure-standard-library, CPU-only realized-cost RLOO advantages, one-batch Bernoulli inverse-probability correction with a lazy whole-batch exact-cost callback, an explicit warm-start boundary, and tiny exact knapsack enumeration. Diagnostics compute observed costs of real feasible decisions for three sampleable parameter predictions, enumerate the score-gradient expectation of two independent categorical samples, and compare it with the analytic gradient. Biased cheap costs are explicit negative-control inputs, not a trained estimator. No LLM, token generation, parameter-JSON parser, H&M pipeline, Adam training, capability evaluation or Evolve operator is supplied. High-cost full experiments are not reproduced; components do not establish capability promotion.

Affected: [Decision-Focused Reinforcement Learning for LLM Post-Training](../../../../post-training/2611.25597-dfrl/README-en.md) · [RLOO](../../../../post-training/2402.14740-rloo/README-en.md)

**2026-11-19** · Fixed-block LCS edit targets, one Ins per gap, no fictitious terminal anchor, mask-threshold fallback, visible-token edit threshold and simultaneous edits followed by truncation/padding. No diffusion forward pass, multi-stage SFT or cycle-resampling decoder. The high-cost full experiment is not reproduced; components or references do not establish capability promotion.

Affected: [Beyond Replacement: Levenshtein Editing for Diffusion Language Models](../../../../post-training/2611.23750-led-edits/README-en.md) · [On-Policy Residual Learning for Diffusion Language Models](../../../../post-training/2610.20687-orl-diffusion/README-en.md)

**2026-11-18** · Review steering-before-GRPO order, separately normalized hint/plain advantages and final-step no-model-update rule; a DPO formula alone is not an implementation. The high-cost full experiment is not reproduced; component diagnostics are not capability comparisons.

Affected: [Get Hint-Augmented GRPO Done Right Through Activation Steering](../../../../post-training/2611.23124-ash-hint-steering/README-en.md) · [DeepSeekMath / GRPO](../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en.md)

**2026-11-18** · Weighted score centers from independent auxiliary actions, detached TIS weights and reverse-KL gradient estimator with an independent KL cap; not reward centering. The high-cost full experiment is not reproduced; component diagnostics are not capability comparisons.

Affected: [Regularized Score Centering](../../../../post-training/2611.21791-regularized-score-centering/README-en.md) · [DeepSeekMath / GRPO](../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en.md)

**2026-11-18** · Centered Gram spectrum of normalized response representations, mass times effective-rank band-pass, denoised LOO-SVD support and two-level RMS advantage calibration. The high-cost full experiment is not reproduced; component diagnostics are not capability comparisons.

Affected: [SpeCal: Spectral Calibration for Unsupervised RLVR](../../../../post-training/2611.20691-specal/README-en.md) · [DeepSeekMath / GRPO](../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en.md)

**2026-11-15** · Add Safety as a Budget to separate advantage scaling from control-level calibration. Only training-limited PAV, two-channel rewards and explicit EMA dual arithmetic are local, not safety training; the high-cost full matrix is not reproduced.

Affected: [Safety as a Budget: Calibrating the Control Channel of Constrained GRPO for Vision-Language Models](../../../../post-training/2611.16628-safety-budget-cgrpo/README-en.md) · [Dr. GRPO](../../../../post-training/2503.20783-dr-grpo/README-en.md)

**2026-11-15** · Add current-likelihood LGPO gating separately from Dr. GRPO advantage scaling. Preserve both advantage signs, token sums and the all-response denominator. Full LLM training is not reproduced due to cost; local gradients are not capability or speed evidence.
